question.:question/problem:
Given that

$$
D=\begin{bmatrix}12 & -3 & 9 \\ 4 & 0 & 3 \\ -4 & 2 & 6\end{bmatrix}
$$

which of the following elementary row operations makes $a_{11}=0$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2}.
$$

At the requested entry, this gives

$$
a_{11}=12+(-3)\cdot (4)=0.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}D &=\begin{bmatrix}12 & -3 & 9 \\ 4 & 0 & 3 \\ -4 & 2 & 6\end{bmatrix}\qquad {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2} \\ &\sim \begin{bmatrix}0 & -3 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 3 \\ -4 & 2 & 6\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2}.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Given that

$$
D=\begin{bmatrix}4 & -3 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 \\ -4 & 2 & 6\end{bmatrix}
$$

which of the following elementary row operations makes $a_{11}=0$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation

$$
{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}.
$$

The entry in row $2$, column $1$ is $0$. Switching rows $1$ and $2$ therefore makes $a_{11}=0$.

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}D &=\begin{bmatrix}4 & -3 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 \\ -4 & 2 & 6\end{bmatrix}\qquad {R}_{1}↔{R}_{2} \\ &\sim \begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 3 \\ 4 & -3 & 9 \\ -4 & 2 & 6\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}.
$$
